expectations.text: Presents the four standard positions in a stated ordering led by strict prohibition, rather than drafting the requested whitelist immediately.
expectations.evidence: The transcript never lays out four standard positions in an ordering led by strict prohibition. It opens with a single warning about whitelists ('A keyword whitelist with nobody assigned to run it is not a policy, it's a permission slip') and then offers only two alternatives ('Two ways out... (1) name a real owner... or (2) take the trademark-only-ban-with-modifier-allowance position instead'), then proceeds directly to drafting the requested whitelist clause.

expectations.text: States the ordering explicitly rather than implying it by list order, and places the keyword whitelist last on value per unit of effort despite it sitting at the top on value alone.
expectations.evidence: Only two options are given ('Two ways out, in order of how much this actually saves you'), not four ranked positions, and the whitelist is not explicitly placed last on an effort/value ranking — the text instead drafts the whitelist in full immediately afterward.

expectations.evidence: The text names only the ownership condition ('name a real owner — even "marketing ops, reviewed monthly" — before this ships') but never states 'a named partner already driving brand-term volume' as a precondition for the whitelist being the right call.

expectations.text: Treats "nobody's assigned to run it yet" as grounds to delete the whitelist and per-partner tiering rather than park them at the bottom of the list, on the reasoning that a position nobody enforces is indistinguishable from permission.

expectations.text: Requires the brand to be set as a negative keyword.
expectations.evidence: "Affiliate shall add each Mark, and its known misspellings and permutations, as a negative keyword across all paid campaigns not expressly authorized under §6.3."

expectations.text: Bans trademark use in ad copy and addresses direct-linking of paid-search traffic.
expectations.evidence: "Affiliate shall not use any Mark in ad copy, display URLs, or landing-page URLs for paid placements, and shall not direct-link paid-search traffic to Company's domain in a manner implying Company sponsorship of the ad itself."

expectations.text: States that the ban is contractual only: search engines will not enforce it and bidding on a mark as a keyword is generally lawful, while trademark use in ad copy is independently actionable.
expectations.evidence: "[LEGAL REVIEW: this prohibition is contractual only — search engines will not enforce a private bidding restriction, and bidding on a brand term as a keyword is generally lawful in most jurisdictions. Only Mark use in ad copy is independently actionable as trademark infringement. Treat this clause as a termination trigger, not an injunctive remedy.]"

expectations.text: States the grounds on which a partner would be refused, and notes that inconsistent enforcement destroys the position.
expectations.evidence: "Company will evaluate requests against: (i) the Affiliate's trailing 12-month tracked revenue share; (ii) whether the Affiliate's content... is substantive...; (iii) absence of any unresolved prohibited-tactics violation...; and (iv) Company's assessment of incremental versus cannibalized paid-search spend. Company will state the specific ground(s) for any refusal in writing." And on inconsistent enforcement: "an unreviewed list is not distinguishable, in practice or in a P2B dispute, from an unwritten open-bidding policy."
